steps.title: Still Doing Great
steps.content:
That's great to hear, {{contact_first_name}}. That's exactly what we hope for when someone finishes care with us. {{provider_name}} will be glad to know you're still doing well.

(Let them respond, then continue.)

steps.title: Ask Permission
steps.content:
While I have you, {{contact_first_name}}, can I ask about a few other areas?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Returning: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to {{complaint_reference}}. First, can I ask about a few other areas?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Questions: Update the File
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Do you have any nagging joint pain?

Any heel or foot pain?

Any tendon trouble?

Is an old injury bothering you?

Do you have any muscle knots?

Any neck or back soreness?

Have you cut back on any activities?

Of those, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Returning: Check Other Areas
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Do you have any nagging joint pain?

Any heel or foot pain?

Any tendon trouble?

Is an old injury bothering you?

Do you have any muscle knots?

Any neck or back soreness?

Have you cut back on any activities?

Between those and the area returning, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Making It Real
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'd like to ask three quick questions about {{main_concern}}.

(Ask each question in order. Let them answer.)

How long has it been bothering you, like a week or two, or longer than that?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "Got it.")

Is it something you experience like 1 to 2 times a month, or is it more often than that?

(Let them answer. If it fits, you can say "I see." or "I understand.")

When it's at its worst, does it ever interfere with work, at home, or relaxing and doing your own thing?

(Let them answer. If they name an impact, reflect only what they said about work, home, or their own time. If not, you can say "Got it, thank you.")

steps.title: The Recommendation
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, that's worth getting looked at instead of just dealing with it. Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get you in so {{provider_name}} can take a look at {{main_concern}}. If acoustic wave therapy can help, we'll walk you through the options. If it's not the right fit, we'll say so. Either way you'll know where you stand. Does that sound reasonable?

(Tap what you hear.)

steps.title: They Hesitate
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I don't want to assume anything. What is holding you back from having {{main_concern}} checked?

(Stay easy about it. Let them answer.)

steps.title: Uncover the Real Concern
steps.content:
Okay, {{contact_first_name}}. I'm not going to push you on it. What's the part giving you pause?

(Let them answer. Then tap what you hear.)

steps.title: Nothing Found: Why They Stopped
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, I'm glad you're still doing well.

Can I ask what changed that led you to stop coming in?

(Let them answer. Do not argue with it.)

Acoustic wave therapy supports healing, but everyday strain can bring problems back. Regular checks help us catch changes early.

(Tap the reason they gave.)

steps.title: They Felt Fine
steps.content:
That makes sense, {{contact_first_name}}. When you feel good, coming back stops feeling urgent. Regular checks help us see whether the area is still doing well.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a check-in on the schedule. Would that be okay?

steps.title: They Mention Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. A check-in is one visit to see how the area is holding. You're not agreeing to more treatment.

(Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts.)

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get that check-in scheduled. Does that seem fair?

steps.title: Life Got Busy
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Life fills up fast, and appointments get pushed down the list. We can find a time that works around your schedule.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's find an easy time for a check-in. Would that work?

steps.title: Waiting for Pain
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Pain can return after the area has been under strain for a while. A check may catch changes before they bother you.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's schedule a quick check. Is that okay?

steps.title: They Moved or Switched
steps.content:
That's understandable, {{contact_first_name}}. Things change. If you're nearby, we'd be glad to see you again. Your treatment history is already in your file.

Was anything else holding you back?

(If they share another reason, tap that reason. Otherwise, continue.)

Can I make a recommendation?

(Wait for the yes.)

Let's get a check-in scheduled. Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Fully Back: Ask Permission
steps.content:
{{contact_first_name}}, we'll come back to {{complaint_reference}}. First, can I ask about a few other areas?

(Wait for the yes.)

steps.title: Fully Back: Check Other Areas
steps.content:
(Write down every area they name.)

{{contact_first_name}}, I'm going to run through a few things people often notice. Just say yes if you get them at all, even if they're mild or come and go.

Do you have any nagging joint pain?

Any heel or foot pain?

Any tendon trouble?

Is an old injury bothering you?

Do you have any muscle knots?

Any neck or back soreness?

Have you cut back on any activities?

Between those and the area fully back, which one bothers you the most?

(Tap their answer below.)

steps.title: Objection: “I thought it was fixed”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Most people finish a series expecting it to hold for good.

Can I ask what's been different since you finished, like more activity, a new job, or more standing?

(Let them answer.)

Your notes say you were moving and feeling better when you finished. So the sessions did their job. The problem is that your day didn't change. The same load kept landing on the same spot. That's why it came back, and it doesn't mean anything failed.

Let's have {{provider_name}} look at what changed. If it's a short top-up, you'll know. If it's something new, you'll know that too.

Would you be open to that?

steps.title: Objection: “It came back”
steps.content:
I'm glad you told me, {{contact_first_name}}. That's one of the most common reasons people call us back.

How long after you stopped did you notice it?

(Let them answer.)

When it comes back that soon, it usually means it was under control but not fully healed. The series stopped a little early, or life pulled on it harder than expected. Either way, it's not you being back at square one. You already did the hard part once.

We'd rather have {{provider_name}} check {{main_concern}} now than let it settle back in. You'll hear where things stand and what it would take.

Can we get you in for a look?

steps.title: Objection: “I manage it myself”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}, and I'm glad it's not stopping you cold.

Can I ask what you're doing for it, like stretching, ice, or something over the counter?

(Let them answer. Give them credit for it.)

Those help, and I'd keep doing them. The thing about managing it is that it's a full-time job. It only holds as long as you keep up with it. The visit is about finding out whether {{main_concern}} still needs managing. There may be a way to get ahead of it instead.

{{provider_name}} can tell you which one it is. If what you're doing is enough, you'll hear that.

Would it help to know for sure?

steps.title: Objection: Injections or Surgery
steps.content:
Okay. That tells me it's gotten bad enough that you want it handled.

Has a doctor recommended that, or is it something you're looking into yourself?

(Let them answer. Do not talk down injections or surgery.)

Both of those are real options, and sometimes they're the right call. They're also hard to undo once you've done them. A visit with {{provider_name}} doesn't rule anything out. It gives you a second look at {{main_concern}} before you commit to something permanent.

If acoustic wave isn't the answer here, we'll say so. Either way you'll walk into that decision knowing more than you do today.

Does it make sense to get that second look first?

steps.title: Objection: “I’m considering another option”
steps.content:
That's fair. Can I ask what you're looking at, like injections, physical therapy, or another office?

(Let them answer. Do not knock the other option.)

Those can all make sense, and some people do well combining them. The part that's hard to compare from home is what would move {{main_concern}} for you. {{provider_name}} already has your history and how you responded to the sessions, so you're not starting over here.

Come in, get a straight answer on where things stand, and then compare. If the other option turns out to be the better fit, you'll be choosing it for a reason.

Is that a fair way to decide?

steps.title: Objection: Cost
steps.content:
I understand, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it the cost of the visit itself, or the thought of paying for a full series again?

(Let them answer. Do not quote prices, packages, or discounts. The office handles that.)

This first visit is one appointment, not a series. You'll hear what anything past that costs before you decide on it. And since you've been here before, we're not starting from scratch, and starting from scratch is the expensive part.

The other side of it is what {{main_concern}} is already costing you, the things you mentioned a minute ago. That's the part I'd hate to see keep adding up.

Can we at least get the look on the calendar?

steps.title: Objection: “I don’t have time”
steps.content:
I hear you, {{contact_first_name}}. Is it finding time for the first visit, or the worry about coming in weekly like before?

(Let them answer.)

Right now we're only talking about one visit. {{provider_name}} looks at {{main_concern}} and tells you what it would take from there. Sometimes that’s a few sessions to settle it down. Sometimes it’s more, and you’ll hear that up front so you can decide. Nobody is signing you up for a series on the phone.

We'll fit that first visit around your schedule, not the other way around.

Could you find a short window for that?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to talk to my spouse”
steps.content:
Of course. Is it more about the money side, or do you two just make these decisions together?

(Let them answer. If it's money, use the cost answer.)

That's fair, and I'm not asking you to commit to anything they'd need to weigh in on. Right now, all you can tell them is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. After the visit, you can tell them what's going on and what it would take. That's an easier conversation to have. And if they'd like to come along, they're welcome.

Can we pencil it in, and you can move it after you two talk?

steps.title: Objection: “I need to think”
steps.content:
That's fair, {{contact_first_name}}. Usually when someone says that, there's one specific thing on their mind. What's the part you'd want to think over?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

Okay. I'm not trying to rush you. The one thing I'd say is that {{main_concern}} is on your mind. It's been that way for a while, and it hasn't sorted itself out on its own. The visit is how you get the information you'd be thinking with. You can think it over just as easily after you know what's going on.

Would it be easier to think it over once you have the answers?

steps.title: Objection: “Send me information”
steps.content:
I can do that, {{contact_first_name}}. What would you want it to cover, so I send the right thing?

(Let them answer. If they name cost, time, or another reason, tap that button.)

I'll be straight with you, though. Anything I send is going to be general. It can't tell you what's realistic for {{main_concern}} specifically. That takes {{provider_name}} seeing you, and that's one short visit.

Let's do both. I'll send the information, and we'll put a time on the calendar. If what I send answers your question, you can call and cancel, no problem.

Does doing both work for you?
